anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 configuration exposes four extraction targets in a five-by-five-by-three pile, with one visible screen and small lava/support/durability parameters, and its browser/grader reduce the action problem to discrete view rotation and mining rays. Polycube Parcel at d4 has no preplaced pieces and requires seven rigid pieces to be oriented and placed into an exact 3x3x3 cover, so it has a larger simultaneous 3D packing search. The Mine has its own dynamic blocker and hazard effects, so this is a qualitative lower-anchor comparison rather than a common-mechanic score.

Polycube success requires every supplied piece to be placed and all 27 cells to be occupied exactly once.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L4/full configuration has a long warehouse route through five barriers with sparse scanners and a hidden die orientation. Its generator solves over position and orientation, the browser rolls the die on movement, and the grader replays the ordered route and timestamps. Polycube d4 is comparable in multi-step full-input burden and planning, but it is a static spatial exact-cover problem with no changing-frame or hidden-orientation memory requirement; its difficulty is concentrated in 3D geometry and collision-dependent cavity planning.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5/simplified configuration requires four accepted swaps on a changing board, an exact target score, at least seven cascade waves, and a refill preview. Each accepted swap changes later board state, and the grader checks the replayed score and wave constraints. Polycube also has state-dependent placement choices because occupancy changes the remaining cavities, but it has no score, wave, move-budget, or forbidden-candy success constraint and accepts any exact cover; this places it below that L5 sequential-constraint anchor while retaining substantial 3D spatial reasoning.

visible_baseline_solution.what_a_screenshot_only_agent_sees: The page shows the task prompt, an isometric SVG parcel with a 3x3x3 gold lattice, seven colored piece entries and their rendered rigid polycubes, occupied-cell and placed-piece counters, the six visible axis-turn buttons, a camera readout, and the mode-specific camera and placement controls. visible_baseline_solution.normal_screenshot_only_solution: A full-mode solution must select a visible loose piece, use the axis buttons to infer and choose a legal 3D orientation, orbit by dragging an empty part of the scene to inspect occluded cells, drag the piece toward a legal lattice location, clear selection, and repeat until all seven pieces fill the 27 cells. The visible browser validates bounds and overlap as placements are made and the direct drag snaps to the nearest projected legal lattice origin. The agent then clicks the visible certification button. Repositioning a placed non-locked piece is available for recovery.
visible_baseline_solution.reasoning_and_memory: The core task is 3D visual understanding plus exact-cover reasoning and planning: each placed piece changes which cavity placements remain legal, and mirrored arms must be distinguished. A normal solution does not need nontrivial temporal memory or a timed action; camera and occupancy are persistent state rather than a changing sequence.
visible_baseline_solution.success_condition: The exported transcript must use the full input sources, include a camera orbit, select and rotate pieces through the visible controls, place every piece legally, clear the final selection, submit as completed, and replay to exact single occupancy of every cell in the 3x3x3 parcel.
visible_baseline_solution.temporal_assessment: The environment declares one frame per observation with a zero-millisecond observation window. The 180-second play-time setting is a resource limit, not a requirement to interpret recent frames; no temporal capability credit is assigned.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The declared L4/full baseline is supported by the actual task: all seven pieces start loose, every legal placement changes the remaining exact-cover cavities, orientations and mirrored shapes must be inferred in 3D, and direct piece/camera dragging adds motor control. findings.claim: The prompt's instruction to inspect the back and, at L5, re-inspect hidden cells after every placement is not enforced as a distinct view-coverage requirement.
findings.causal_explanation: The browser records a camera_orbit event after any qualifying direct drag or any proxy camera button. The grader checks only that at least one in-range camera event occurred, then checks final occupancy; it does not require a rear-facing angle, repeated re-inspection, or any camera-dependent placement evidence. Thus the wording contributes little graded difficulty beyond one camera event.

evidence.explanation: The d4 and d5 natural-language contracts explicitly require inspecting the back, with d5 requiring re-inspection after every placement.

findings.recommended_action: If rear inspection is intended to carry difficulty credit, add a narrowly specified camera-coverage or camera-dependent evidence check. Otherwise treat that wording as guidance and do not count repeated inspection as an enforced difficulty feature.

findings.claim: Full-mode placement is nearest-valid-origin snap assistance rather than a visually exact drop onto the intended lattice cell.
findings.causal_explanation: The browser enumerates every currently valid integer origin, chooses the one whose projected centroid is nearest to the release point, and accepts it whenever the nearest candidate is within 105 screen units. The independent grader requires a finite drag path and a legal after_origin, but does not compare the release coordinate to the selected origin. This does not bypass exact-cover or collision reasoning, but it makes full placement less precision-demanding than the direct-drag wording suggests and differs from simplified selectors in control granularity.

evidence.explanation: bestDrop searches all valid origins and selects the closest projected candidate.
A full drop is accepted when the nearest candidate is no more than 105 units away, then the browser records that legal origin.
The grader checks path shape and legal replay state but has no release-coordinate-to-origin correspondence check.

findings.recommended_action: Document the full surface as snap-assisted, or tighten the tolerance and grade a destination correspondence if precise visual dropping is intended; preserve the same legal occupancy effects across modes.

L5 lowers parcel opacity, raises piece opacity, tightens rack spacing, and changes the starting camera, which can make hidden cavities and piece separation harder but can also have mixed visual effects. Whether this is a sufficient L5 step cannot be established from source alone.

findings.recommended_action: Keep L5 as a candidate presentation-hard profile, but calibrate screenshot usability and completion performance against L4 before treating the separation as an established level boundary.

concise_summary: Keep Polycube Parcel at its declared L4/full baseline. The source implements a seven-piece 3D exact-cover problem whose placements change later legal cavities, placing it above the approved L1 Mine and qualitatively alongside the approved L4 Blind Dice Courier, while the approved L5 Candy Cascade has stronger sequential score and board-change constraints. The five profiles are active and mostly ordered; L4-to-L5 is a visual-only step needing calibration. The camera-inspection wording is not enforced beyond one camera event, and full drops use broad nearest-valid-origin snapping.
limitations: This was a source-only audit; no browser, screenshot, VNC, human, or agent run was performed.
No historical pre-controls implementation or fixed-seed artifact was available for a preservation diff.
Anchor comparisons are qualitative because the anchors use different mechanics and no common empirical performance data was available.
The bundled private solver was treated as implementation evidence only; the visible-baseline description is based on the rendered controls and grader contract.
